meta.scratchpad: The four 2026-04-19 reference screenshots are now the canonical UI target for both sketch and whiteboard. Prior close-out on the shell/design tranche overstated progress: the current branch has partial infrastructure, but it does not yet match the screenshot composition, surface language, or turn-log presentation. Reopening the screenshot-parity rows and deferring the generic readiness audit because the immediate job is direct convergence to the provided images.

tasks.title: Phase 1: Canvas connection overlay foundation
tasks.goal: Render existing Connection records directly on the canvas as a bounded SVG overlay so relationships are visible without opening the drawer.
tasks.comment: Claiming Phase 1 foundation work.
definition_of_done: Canvas renders up to 8-10 high-signal connections with style by kind.
Connected line endpoints update while an attached idea is being dragged.
Clicking a connection line highlights both endpoint ideas without breaking drag, group, or merge flows.
constraints: Reuse existing Connection records; do not introduce a new persisted connection model.
Keep the overlay non-intrusive and preserve current canvas interactions.

context.notes: Canvas now renders a bounded SVG connection overlay with drag-aware endpoints and click-to-highlight behavior.

tasks.title: Phase 1: Add draw_connection WebMCP tool
tasks.goal: Expose a WebMCP tool that creates a visible connection between two ideas in one call and routes through the same app state used by the canvas overlay.
tasks.comment: Keep this tool aligned with the existing dispatch-and-wait tool path; agents should be able to narrate and render the link in one action.
definition_of_done: A global draw_connection tool is registered and documented alongside find_connections.
Calling the tool results in a visible connection on the canvas.
Tool output clearly reports what was connected and how it was classified.
constraints: Do not add hidden coupling between the tool and future critique/timing systems.
Preserve the existing StrictMode-safe registration pattern.

context.notes: draw_connection is registered as a global WebMCP tool and threads through app-owned board connection state.

tasks.title: Phase 2: Persisted critique system
tasks.goal: Add the critique storage, WebMCP tools, and anchored critique-card UI so the app can challenge ideas sharply without interrupting flow.
tasks.comment: There is already a devilsAdvocate role in the phase pipeline, but this phase requires a separate persisted critique system with its own store, tools, and card UI.
definition_of_done: Critiques persist in a dedicated store and survive reloads.
critique_idea, list_critiques, and dismiss_critique are exposed through WebMCP.
Critique cards anchor near the target idea and never block interaction.
constraints: Critiques must appear only after idle and must not spam the board.
Critique phrasing should be sharp and specific rather than generic.

context.notes: Persisted critiques now have a dedicated IDB store, anchored canvas cards, and critique/list/dismiss WebMCP tools.

tasks.title: Phase 3: Soft mode inference timing layer
tasks.goal: Infer whether the board is exploring, structuring, stressing, or converging, then time AI actions subtly without adding explicit mode toggles.
tasks.comment: This phase should control timing, not decision authority. The UI cue must be subtle and fade if ignored.
definition_of_done: A lightweight inferredMode classifier exists with a reason and confidence.
Mode output drives the appropriate non-blocking suggestion or tool trigger path.
No mode toggle is added to the UI.
constraints: Never interrupt typing or dragging.
Only act after idle and never force a mode switch.

context.notes: Starting the timing layer after syncing completed facilitator slices.

tasks.title: Phase 4: Signal control and noise reduction
tasks.goal: Bound critiques, suggestions, and connections so the system stays trustworthy as more autonomous behavior lands.
tasks.comment: Do not scale broken signal. Thresholding and cooldowns should come after the underlying connection and critique signals are correct.
definition_of_done: Connection confidence threshold is enforced.
Per-idea critique cooldown prevents spam.
Suggestion deduplication and visible-count bounds keep the canvas clean.
constraints: Maximum 2 critiques per idea, 6 visible suggestions, and 10 connections total.
Keep all control logic aligned with the existing live board state.

tasks.title: Phase 5: Turn-log pagination
tasks.goal: Split large turn-log payloads out of get_idea so debugging and agent inspection scale without oversized responses.
tasks.comment: This is the observability sidecar the roadmap calls out for future connectionFinder and devilsAdvocate turn-log growth.
definition_of_done: get_turn_log returns paginated entries with nextCursor.
get_idea returns turn-log summary metadata instead of the full array.
Agent-side inspection can retrieve history incrementally.
constraints: Do not lose existing turn-log data.
Keep the new tool shape consistent with current WebMCP tool conventions.

tasks.title: Phase 6: Local autonomous facilitator
tasks.goal: Add bounded observer-driven automation so the system can add value without explicit user commands and without overwhelming the user.
tasks.comment: This remains local-only and should not start until the earlier facilitator phases are stable.
definition_of_done: State-change observers trigger bounded tool actions under explicit safeguards.
A global pause toggle exists.
AI-originated actions are tagged so the user can distinguish them from direct edits.
constraints: No sync or Yjs work starts here.
Human interruptibility must remain immediate.

tasks.title: Phase 7: Demo polish
tasks.goal: Refine animation timing, transitions, and layout so the facilitator behaviors read as intentional and impressive during the demo.
tasks.comment: This closes the sequence only after the earlier functional phases are working and stable.
definition_of_done: Connection, critique, and suggestion moments animate smoothly.
UI transitions avoid abrupt jumps.
The board reads as polished on desktop and mobile.
constraints: Do not hide unresolved functional issues with polish work.
Preserve the existing visual language rather than replacing it.

tasks.title: 4.1 Two-tab BroadcastChannel + Yjs sync spike
tasks.goal: Prove zero-server two-tab sync by wrapping the ideas store in a Y.Map with BroadcastChannel transport and y-indexeddb persistence.
tasks.comment: Closed after tightening the web consumer seam around the existing Yjs ideas sync: board-scoped ideasChanged handling, ideas-only reload path, and display-group reconciliation from synced panel.groupId state.
definition_of_done: Adding an idea in tab A appears in tab B in under 100ms on the same machine.
The ideas store is backed by a Y.Map with BroadcastChannel transport.
Reload preserves shared state through y-indexeddb while docs, suggestions, and groups stay IDB-only.
constraints: Do not start full-store Yjs migration in this slice.
Keep the spike isolated to the ideas store and validate concurrent panel-drag merge behavior.

context.notes: Verified with npm run typecheck and npm run build:web. The repo already had the Yjs/BroadcastChannel/y-indexeddb ideas backend; this slice narrowed the web refresh seam and kept cross-tab group visuals coherent without migrating docs/suggestions/groups out of IDB.

tasks.title: 4.2 Full CRDT port for board stores
tasks.goal: Replace direct IDB writes across board stores with Y.Doc-backed mutations and ship a one-shot migration path from existing local data.
tasks.comment: Yjs is a storage rewrite, not a feature flag, so the port layer must hide the backend from UI and tool code.
definition_of_done: Storage helpers route through Y.Doc-backed mutations across the board stores.
First boot after upgrade migrates existing IDB data into the Y.Doc once.
UI and WebMCP tools operate unchanged through the storage port layer.
constraints: Do not keep a parallel IDB plus Yjs write path.
Migration must preserve existing board data and avoid two sources of truth.

context.notes: This follows the two-tab spike and should stay behind a clean storage port.

tasks.title: 4.3 WebRTC cross-machine sync with SDP-only broker
tasks.goal: Extend collaborative sync across machines by swapping BroadcastChannel transport for y-webrtc and adding the minimal SDP-broker room flow.
tasks.comment: The broker may pass SDP offers only; it must never carry Y.Doc payload.
definition_of_done: Peers can join a room across machines using a short room code or invite URL.
Remote sync uses y-webrtc instead of BroadcastChannel.
The signaling path carries SDP offers only and keeps idea payloads peer-to-peer.
constraints: Do not ship manual token-paste signaling.
Keep the broker minimal and avoid central storage of board contents.

context.notes: The roadmap explicitly rejects manual token-paste signaling even as a stopgap.

tasks.title: 4.4 CRDT-driven autonomous facilitator triggers
tasks.goal: Move facilitator triggers onto Y.Doc update events with idle gating, AI-host election, and AI-origin dedup so exactly one peer automates the board.
tasks.comment: Claiming the current critical-path automation task; splitting implementation and validation across high-effort agents.
definition_of_done: The observer subscribes to Y.Doc update events rather than local-only board state.
Exactly one peer claims AI-host responsibility via awareness-based election.
AI-originated transactions are tagged and deduped across peers.
constraints: Preserve global pause and bounded automation behavior.
Avoid duplicate ghost panels or repeated role runs during split-brain or host handoff.

context.notes: Peer-aware automation starts only after sync is real.

tasks.notes: Completed bo-012 against the current repo sync stack. The observer now waits on sync-derived board changes instead of local-only activity, tracks newly seen ideas for connect/scout trigger queues, prefers phase-4+ critique targets with no active critique, and uses deterministic `automationKey` values on automatic scout/critique commits so storage dedupes split-brain races per target instead of by text alone. Host election remains the repo's existing lowest-live-client facilitator heartbeat path rather than a new `y-protocols/awareness` dependency, but exactly one peer still hosts at a time. Verification: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build:web`.

tasks.title: Stretch: search_local_docs local RAG tool
tasks.goal: Let the user grant a local docs folder and search PRDs/specs with File System Access-backed local retrieval surfaced as supporting-doc candidates or scout context.
tasks.comment: Closed with an explicit local-doc candidate tool flow layered onto the existing DocsModal grant/search/attach UX. search_local_docs now returns candidates or re-authorize guidance, and attach_local_doc_candidate turns a chosen hit into a normal supporting doc that feeds later scout context.
definition_of_done: A user can grant a folder and issue local doc searches from the app.
Matches surface as supporting-doc candidates or scout context rather than opaque raw snippets.
The app has a deliberate re-authorize flow for per-session permission loss.
constraints: Do not hide the File System Access permission boundary.
Do not assume persistent folder grants across reloads.

context.notes: The repo already had the File System Access UI path in DocsModal. This slice added the missing board-first WebMCP tool surface and corrected the supporting-doc tool completion shape to use docId rather than id.

tasks.title: Stretch: cross_pollinate role and tool
tasks.goal: Introduce a dedicated cross_pollinate role that finds two distinct ideas and proposes a third merged concept with clearer intent than scout_ideas.
tasks.comment: Completed the dedicated cross_pollinate role and tool slice with explicit source-idea attribution on persisted suggestions.
definition_of_done: A dedicated cross_pollinate role exists with structured output.
A WebMCP tool exposes the role on the standalone board surface.
The resulting suggestion clearly attributes the two source ideas it combines.
constraints: Do not duplicate scout_ideas behavior without a sharper synthesis contract.
Keep the output anchored to existing ideas rather than free-floating unrelated suggestions.

context.notes: The role now returns a strict two-idea source pair, the WebMCP surface exposes cross_pollinate separately from scout_ideas, and persisted suggestions carry sourceIdeaIds for explicit attribution.

tasks.title: Stretch: declarative WebMCP + toolautosubmit
tasks.goal: Add agent-aware declarative form fields that emit tool calls on change when Chrome preview support is good enough.
tasks.comment: Deferred after repo audit and Chrome/WebMCP doc check: the codebase has no declarative form/toolautosubmit path, detectWebMcpSupport currently only assumes declarative support when navigator.modelContext exists, and ROADMAP.md/WEBMCP_CAPABILITIES.md still treat Chrome 146 preview validation as an open prerequisite. Leaving this closed as externally blocked until real preview validation exists.
definition_of_done: Declarative form fields can emit tool calls on change for supported surfaces.
The implementation is validated against the Chrome preview requirements called out in the WebMCP docs.
Unsupported environments degrade cleanly without breaking existing manual tools.
constraints: Do not ship this before preview validation is real.
Keep HTTP and manual tool invocation paths working without declarative support.

context.notes: Roadmap explicitly marks this as blocked on Chrome 146 preview validation.

tasks.blocker_reason: Blocked on real Chrome/WebMCP preview validation for declarative form tools and toolautosubmit; current repo support is imperative-only and local detection overstates declarative capability.

tasks.title: Stretch: multi-user facilitator UX
tasks.goal: Once sync is real, add speaker tracking, consensus summaries, and end-of-session action-item capture that make facilitator behavior legible in collaborative sessions.
tasks.comment: Completed shared-session facilitator UX. The companion rail now surfaces a Shared facilitator card only in multi-peer sessions, with active peers, recent-floor speaker tracking, a consensus pulse derived from recent session events, and facilitator-owned action items. Shared sync now persists a bounded recentSessionEvents window with peer attribution and summaries. Verified with npm run typecheck and npm run build:web.
definition_of_done: Collaborative sessions surface facilitator-owned consensus summaries and action items.
The UX is designed for multi-user sessions rather than single-user board nudges.
The feature reads as an extension of the shared facilitator rather than a separate tool silo.
constraints: Do not start before sync and peer-aware facilitator plumbing are stable.
Keep the facilitator non-intrusive even in active discussions.

context.notes: This is explicitly downstream of the collaborative sync track.

tasks.title: Stretch: W1 external system integration tools
tasks.goal: Use the W1 active-tab tool path to let phase transitions write to Linear, Jira, or PRD tools with explicit second-step consent.
tasks.comment: This should extend the existing W1 consume path rather than invent a separate integration channel.
definition_of_done: The app can chain active-tab tool writes into supported external systems.
Phase-transition writeback requires an explicit second consent step.
The integration reuses existing W1 patterns instead of introducing a parallel bridge.
constraints: Do not bypass explicit consent for external writes.
Preserve the existing active-tab consumption architecture.

context.notes: This is the explicit W1 writeback stretch item from the roadmap.

tasks.notes: Implemented in commit c1c4ff8 via the existing W1 consume path. Phase and next-step changes now surface a second-consent writeback draft in the live-tool panel, with editable JSON payloads and an active-origin guard before invokeActiveTabTool(). Verification: npm run typecheck, npm run build:web.

tasks.title: 3.1 Visual hierarchy pass
tasks.goal: Make the current canvas instantly legible by establishing one active focus, stronger structure weighting, critique dominance, and slight de-emphasis of irrelevant ideas.
tasks.comment: Start with hierarchy before animation so the board has a stable visual grammar.
definition_of_done: Exactly one idea can read as active at a time through subtle elevation and accent treatment.
Strongest connections render with the clearest weight while secondary structure fades to roughly 60-70% opacity.
Critique cards visually outrank structure without covering or blocking their target ideas.
constraints: Do not add new UI surfaces or persistent clutter.
Maintain readability on dense boards and keep non-active ideas above readability thresholds.

context.notes: The board should tell the user what matters before any new motion layer is added.

tasks.title: 3.2 Motion design and reveal animation
tasks.goal: Make connections, critiques, suggestions, and highlight feedback animate with directional, idle-gated motion that feels intentional rather than abrupt.
tasks.comment: Directional motion should explain what just happened without becoming theatrical.
definition_of_done: Connections draw from source to target over roughly 300-500ms with stroke-dash animation.
Critiques enter with a 10-20px offset and 200-300ms fade-slide after idle.
Suggestions and connection-click highlights follow the same motion language and timing band.
constraints: Never animate during drag or typing.
Support reduced-motion fallbacks without losing state clarity.

context.notes: Motion needs to read as explanation, not decoration.

tasks.title: 3.3 Sequential idle-gated facilitator timing
tasks.goal: Resequence facilitator output so the board reveals one structural insight, then one critique, then later a suggestion only after a stable idle window.
tasks.comment: The magic layer is sequencing, cancellation, and patience rather than more output.
definition_of_done: Idle detection waits roughly 1.2-2.0 seconds after the last interaction before showing anything.
Queued AI actions reveal one at a time with 600-1000ms spacing in the order connection, critique, suggestion.
Any user interaction cancels pending AI reveals and resets timing cleanly.
constraints: Do not allow simultaneous insight reveals.
Do not interrupt typing, drag, dismiss, or edit flows.

context.notes: This is the patience layer that prevents the facilitator from feeling noisy or random.

tasks.title: 3.4 Signal control and overflow refinement
tasks.goal: Keep the facilitator trustworthy by enforcing hard visible limits, hiding weak signals, and collapsing overflow without adding new panels.
tasks.comment: Do not scale broken signal; show fewer, stronger insights and degrade overflow gracefully.
definition_of_done: Visible output stays within the roadmap bounds for connections, critiques per idea, and suggestions.
Weak connections are filtered out entirely while secondary but valid signals de-emphasize smoothly.
Suggestion overflow collapses into an existing-surface '+N more' affordance rather than a new panel.
constraints: Apply limits without making data disappear abruptly.
Use confidence and rank ordering rather than FIFO truncation.

context.notes: The board should stay clean even when the facilitator has more candidate output.

tasks.title: 3.5 Micro-interactions and board responsiveness
tasks.goal: Add subtle drag, hover, edit, and grouping reactions that make the current board feel aware and alive without increasing noise.
tasks.comment: These reactions should reward attention and preserve calm, not create constant motion.
definition_of_done: Nearby connections react smoothly during drag with light elastic tension instead of rigid snapping.
Critiques soften during edits and regain full presence after idle returns.
Hovering an idea highlights related connections and critiques as one coherent set.
constraints: Avoid jitter under high-frequency drag updates.
Do not let hover or edit feedback fight the idle-gated reveal queue.

context.notes: Responsiveness matters, but the board still has to feel calm and deliberate.

tasks.title: 3.6 Critique tone and language tightening
tasks.goal: Reshape critique output so every card sounds like a sharp collaborator using brief, direct challenge language instead of generic summaries.
tasks.comment: The critique voice should increase trust by being concise, pointed, and obviously actionable.
definition_of_done: Critiques bias toward direct formulations such as 'This fails if...' and 'You're assuming...'.
Each critique fits within 2-3 short lines without long passive summary paragraphs.
Persisted and regenerated critiques both respect the same terse copy standard.
constraints: Do not let prompt shaping regress critique specificity.
Do not exceed the existing card footprint.

context.notes: Sharper language is part of perceived intelligence, not just copy polish.

tasks.title: 3.7 Final consistency and demo-quality polish
tasks.goal: Unify spacing, easing, durations, and color discipline across the existing facilitator surfaces so the whole experience reads as one intentional system.
tasks.comment: This closes the polish driver only after hierarchy, motion, timing, and tone are already aligned.
definition_of_done: Connection, critique, and suggestion surfaces share the same 200-500ms timing band and ease-out motion language.
Spacing and alignment feel consistent across desktop and narrow viewport layouts.
Color discipline stays strict: critique in red/orange, structure in blue/grey, suggestions in teal.
constraints: Do not paper over unresolved interaction bugs with visual polish.
Keep the current product shape rather than redesigning it.

context.notes: The close-out pass should make the demo feel smooth, deliberate, and premium.

tasks.title: Design Core: board document and board-scoped repositories
tasks.goal: Replace the web app's phase-first hot path with a canonical board document and board-scoped stores for boards, ideas, connections, critiques, turns, and tweaks, with a migration bridge from existing local data.
tasks.comment: Starting board-first domain and board-scoped repository cutover from the Integration Guide target state.
definition_of_done: A canonical Board document or aggregate exists and the web app reads board-scoped state from it.
IndexedDB stores cover boards, ideas, connections, critiques, turns, and tweaks through one hydration path.
Legacy phase fields are isolated behind an adapter so the board path stops depending on Idea.phase in the hot path.
constraints: Do not keep two durable sources of truth for the same board entities.
Migration must preserve existing local board data and current web app startup behavior.

context.notes: Completed the board-first repository cutover for the standalone web app: App now hydrates from a board repository snapshot, workspace phase rendering is isolated behind a legacy adapter, and WebMCP lifecycle tools consume a legacy tool projection instead of the raw selected board idea.

tasks.title: Design Core: patch journal and reversible BoardController
tasks.goal: Route all committed board mutations through a central BoardController that emits forward and inverse JSON patches, persists ChangeSets, and becomes the only mutation path for user and AI actions.
tasks.comment: Completed the live journal cutover: committed board mutations across the web app, WebMCP tools, workspace shell, sidepanel consent/create flows, and fallback forms now route through the boardController changeSet path, with dead compatibility writes removed from the board repository. Verification: npm run typecheck passes; vite builds remain blocked by local ENOSPC on dist outputs.
definition_of_done: All committed board mutations route through a single applyChange or equivalent mutation API.
ChangeSets persist forward and inverse JSON patches with actor, summary, and affected entity metadata.
Undo and redo replay the journal rather than rebuilding state ad hoc from UI handlers.
constraints: Human and AI changes must share the same journal semantics.
Ephemeral beat drafts must stay separate from committed board state until the user keeps them or automation is explicitly allowed.

context.notes: This is the mechanism behind undo/redo, change history, and reversible AI structural edits.

tasks.title: Design Core: beat runtime and proposal contract
tasks.goal: Replace the current web-app phase loop with a board-level callBeat runtime for scout, connect, critique, cluster, and summarise, using strict JSON beat outputs and candidate proposals instead of direct structural writes.
tasks.comment: Completed the beat runtime/proposal contract slice. Added `src/beats/types.ts`, `src/orchestrator/beatRegistry.ts`, `src/orchestrator/runBeat.ts`, and `apps/web/beatContext.ts`; introduced the `boardSummariser` role; routed the live scout/connect/critique paths in `apps/web/App.tsx` through typed beat envelopes before commit; surfaced active beat state in the header; and tightened `ChangeActor.beat` typing. Verification: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build:web`, and `npm run build` all pass.
definition_of_done: The web path exposes exactly five beats: scout, connect, critique, cluster, and summarise.
Each beat returns strict JSON with candidates, sources, confidence metadata, and patch payloads or equivalent change intents.
Automatic and manual beat triggers are encoded with visible state for small versus big beats.
constraints: Do not let freeform AI responses mutate board structure directly.
Retain narrow role prompts and machine-parseable outputs for every beat.

context.notes: This is the contract shift from phase progression to board beats.

tasks.title: Design Core: board-first WebMCP surface
tasks.goal: Retarget the existing WebMCP boundary around board verbs and beat runs instead of legacy phase and workspace concepts, while keeping the direct web app WebMCP integration.
tasks.comment: Completed the board-first WebMCP surface cut. Added `get_board` and `run_beat` to `apps/web/webmcp-tools.ts`, wired `brainstorm:runBeat` handling in `apps/web/App.tsx`, and demoted the legacy phase-local WebMCP lifecycle registrations so the active surface is board-first and beat-first. Verification: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build:web`, and `npm run build` all pass.
definition_of_done: Board tools cover the board document, beat invocation, candidate admission or dismissal, and connection or critique operations through the board controller.
dispatch-and-wait or equivalent request handling stays intact for the standalone web app.
Tool handlers operate on current board and beat-run state rather than phase-local state.
constraints: Keep the direct WebMCP surface; do not add a second UI abstraction layer such as a2ui.
Do not duplicate orchestration logic across App state and tool handlers.

context.notes: This preserves WebMCP while aligning it to the guide's board and beat model.

tasks.title: Design Core: extract board shell from apps/web/App.tsx
tasks.goal: Break the monolithic App.tsx into board controller, storage sync, beat orchestration, and inspector modules so board-first behavior is testable and the workspace drawer stops owning the hot path.
tasks.comment: Verified complete against current code: App.tsx is orchestration-only, BoardAppView owns the shell, and workspace surfaces are overlay-secondary rather than the hot path.
definition_of_done: App.tsx no longer owns history mutation logic, storage choreography, facilitator timing, and layout concerns in one file.
Board controller and board UI hooks have explicit boundaries and callers.
Workspace surfaces remain available as secondary inspector or export views rather than primary orchestration surfaces.
constraints: Preserve current app boot, tool registration, and board interaction behavior while extracting modules.
Do not strand dead code paths behind the old workspace-first model.

context.notes: Tracker references were stale to the pre-extraction App.tsx shape. The current board-first shell already satisfies the slice.

tasks.title: Design Core: durable turns, tweaks, tombstones, and reversible deletes
tasks.goal: Complete the persistence layer for beat runs, turn history, tweak state, and tombstones so dismissed AI outputs remain reversible and history-backed instead of being hard-deleted or left in transient component state.
tasks.comment: Persistence now includes a journal-backed tweak mutation path, legacy tweak migration, and a web-safe settings path that no longer depends on shimmed chrome.storage for the web app.
definition_of_done: Turns, beat runs, tweak state, and tombstones persist in board-scoped storage.
Dismissed or deleted AI artifacts are represented as reversible tombstones rather than silent hard deletes.
Web settings or tweak persistence no longer depend on chrome.storage.local for the web path without a compatible abstraction.
constraints: Do not lose existing local settings or board data during the storage move.
History data must stay compatible with undo and redo semantics from the patch journal.

context.notes: Landed durable tweak storage on the same board history path as other board mutations, exposed it to the web app, and aligned the web options/settings copy with the IndexedDB-backed store.

tasks.title: Design UI: always-on Dev companion and idle-triggered beats
tasks.goal: Make the Dev companion visibly present while the user edits the board, with automatic idle-triggered runs, explicit watching or drafting states, and visible beat activity when something big is happening or the user asks for it.
tasks.comment: The inline Dev companion now shows watching, primed, paused, drafting, and big-beat states tied to meaningful board changes while preserving typing/drag interruptibility.
definition_of_done: The board shows companion presence and state while the user is editing or when beats are running.
Automatic beat triggering is idle-gated and tied to meaningful board changes.
Big beats can reveal active beat progress and interim idea or source discovery state without forcing it on every small edit.
constraints: Do not interrupt active editing or hijack focus while the user is typing or dragging.
Preserve human interruptibility and global pause behavior.

context.notes: Automatic beats now idle-gate on the latest meaningful board change rather than coarse wall-clock idleness alone, and the companion surfaces pending-change countdowns plus persisted pause state.

tasks.title: Design UI: beat review flow with keep or scratch candidates
tasks.goal: Surface big-beat outputs as reviewable candidate ideas, sources, connections, critiques, and structural edits that the user can keep or scratch individually or as a group before they become committed board changes.
tasks.comment: Completed the beat review flow: cluster/summarise runs now create durable review sessions/items in board state; keep/scratch decisions are journaled and undoable; the app renders a centered review panel with provenance, affected ideas/structures, and per-item or batch keep/scratch controls; kept cluster hints also apply existing group/theme mutations. Verification: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build:web` pass.
definition_of_done: Beat review UI shows candidate items with provenance, summaries, and the affected ideas or structures.
Keep commits the candidate into the board journal; scratch creates a tombstone and preserves the decision in history.
Users can accept a subset of a beat without discarding the rest of the run.
constraints: Do not auto-commit structural AI edits without an explicit keep path or a narrowly defined low-risk automation rule.
Dismissed items must remain recoverable through history rather than disappearing silently.

context.notes: Matches the requested keep or scratch flow for beats and candidate ideas.

tasks.title: Design UI: undo or redo controls and change history timeline
tasks.goal: Add visible undo and redo controls plus a readable change history that groups user and AI changes by actor, beat, and patch set so the board can move backward and forward safely.
tasks.comment: Completed the visible history slice: undo/redo remain in the header, the board now loads live ChangeSets alongside cursor state, and a floating history panel shows actor, beat, summary, timestamp, status, patch count, and affected entities for each durable ChangeSet. Verification: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build:web` pass.
definition_of_done: Undo and redo controls are visible and operate across user and AI-authored changes.
A history surface shows actor, beat, summary, timestamp, and affected board entities for each ChangeSet.
Moving backward and forward preserves board consistency and does not drop persisted state.
constraints: Do not fall back to snapshot-only history that loses semantic change information.
Guard against replaying inverse patches against the wrong board revision.

context.notes: Implements the user-visible history and navigation controls requested for patch-backed state.

tasks.title: Design UI: board-first layout cutover and inline AI surfaces
tasks.goal: Make the canvas the primary product surface, move workspace detail into a secondary inspector role, and replace the remaining workspace-first interaction path with inline board-native AI affordances.
tasks.comment: Completed the board-first layout cutover: selecting an idea now opens a centered board-focus dock that hosts the live phase loop and inline tool context; the old workspace is now an explicit secondary inspector; the shell keeps review, history, capture, and docs compatible with the board-first flow. Verification: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build:web` pass.
definition_of_done: Primary brainstorm flow happens on the board with inline AI artifacts and review surfaces.
Workspace or drawer surfaces are secondary inspectors, not the place where the main loop lives.
No sidebar-chat style surface becomes the primary AI interaction model.
constraints: Preserve desktop and mobile usability while moving controls onto the board.
Do not regress current board interactions such as drag, grouping, or selection.

context.notes: Board selection now drives a board-native focus dock, while the inspector is explicit and secondary.

tasks.title: Design UI: cluster and summarise beats
tasks.goal: Implement the missing cluster and summarise beats with inline group proposals, board-level thematic labeling, and summaries that stay connected to board entities and beat history.
tasks.comment: Completed the cluster and summarise beat slice: cluster now uses a dedicated boardClusterer role that can return multiple inline grouping proposals from shared-theme components; summarise now receives live group themes/questions and emits explicit related group ids; review items and history entries carry the actual takeaway text plus labeled idea/group provenance. Verification: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build:web` pass.
definition_of_done: Cluster beat can propose grouping or regrouping operations with user review.
Summarise beat produces board-level digests tied back to ideas, sources, or groups.
Both beats show up in beat history and use the same proposal and keep or scratch contract as the rest of the system.
constraints: Do not ship cluster or summary behavior as ad hoc side effects outside the beat runtime.
Summaries must reference real board entities rather than floating free text alone.

context.notes: Closes the missing beat gap between the current app and the target interaction model.

tasks.title: Design UI: source-linked metadata edits and structural idea operations
tasks.goal: Let kept beat candidates append metadata to existing ideas, attach sources, create entirely new ideas, rewrite idea structure, or modify existing relationships while preserving provenance and reversibility.
tasks.comment: Completed source-linked metadata and structural review operations: summary review now yields structured `idea_insight` and `idea_spawn` candidates, keep actions dispatch through board-controller mutations instead of no-op bookkeeping, and ideas now carry durable `insights` metadata with linked source refs surfaced in the canvas/inspector. Cluster hints continue to handle reversible structural edits through the same review path. Verification: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build:web` pass.
definition_of_done: Accepted candidates can create new ideas, enrich existing idea metadata, attach sources, or modify structure through the board controller.
Every structural edit retains provenance and remains reversible through the patch journal.
The board can represent changed idea structure without losing the prior state or source linkage.
constraints: Do not treat source attachment or structure edits as opaque text blobs.
All structural AI edits must be attributable and reversible.

context.notes: Implements the user's requirement that kept beats can enrich, create, or restructure board ideas.

tasks.title: Design UI: final integration-guide fidelity and accessibility pass
tasks.goal: Align the shipped experience with the guide's intended visual language, reveal choreography, accessibility, theme behavior, and empty or loading states once the board-first interaction model is in place.
tasks.comment: Completed the final guide-fidelity pass with persisted theme switching, reduced-motion support, dialog-style history/review overlays, and more intentional board-first empty plus review states.
definition_of_done: Theme and motion behavior align with the guide across sketch and whiteboard modes.
Keyboard, focus, and screen-reader behaviors cover the new inline AI and history surfaces.
Empty, loading, thinking, kept, and scratched states feel intentional rather than bolted on.
constraints: Do not trade away board responsiveness for decorative polish.
Avoid generic assistant UI patterns that conflict with the design guide's visual direction.

context.notes: This pass added persisted whiteboard/sketch theme state, board-surface theming via body data attributes, reduced-motion handling for visible beat animations, and keyboard/screen-reader treatment for review/history overlays.

tasks.title: Design UI: replace the rail shell with canvas-first chrome
tasks.goal: Restructure the shell around the freeform canvas, compact topbar tools, a reserved peer-presence slot, a bead-strip home, and a bottom-left persona/discard zone so the app no longer depends on a persistent facilitator rail.
tasks.comment: The shell must leave durable spatial homes for the bead strip, persona dock, discard pile, turn log, and future peer chips. If those surfaces require a later relayout, the shell is still wrong.
definition_of_done: The canvas is the primary screen surface with no persistent facilitator/chat rail dominating the layout.
The chrome matches the reference structure: compact topbar tools, board-title chip, and a bottom-left persona dock.
The shell reserves spatial homes for the bead strip, discard pile, turn log, and a hidden top-right peer chip row without needing another layout rewrite later.
Primary AI controls remain accessible without requiring users to discover a secondary side panel.
constraints: Do not preserve the current right-rail architecture as the main interaction model.
Do not solve this by shrinking or polishing the rail further; the structure itself must move toward the reference design.
Do not hide future collaboration/autonomy surfaces in settings or modals because the shell failed to make room for them.

context.notes: Partial shell cutover landed, but the current board still does not match the screenshot layout: wrong chrome composition, wrong spacing/density, and missing the strong centered-title / top-right tool-cluster composition visible in the references.

tasks.notes: Partial slice landed: the rail now prioritizes the facilitator, Scout, and Board Beats before the heavier connection/session surfaces, and the facilitator deck is visually compressed instead of being dominated by diagnostics. Real viewport proof is still required before closing this task.

tasks.title: Design UI: make note capture viewport-aware and visibly successful
tasks.goal: Ensure creating a note is an above-fold primary action and that a successful create always reveals the new idea where the user is actually looking.
tasks.comment: The reference design wants add-note and AI output to create real stickies on the canvas, not succeed silently behind chrome or off-screen.
definition_of_done: There is a clear add-note entrypoint in primary chrome, not just a floating affordance that competes with other overlays.
New notes are placed relative to the current viewport or the canvas automatically pans or centers to the created note.
Successful creation produces immediate visual confirmation and failures surface inline instead of only logging to the console.
constraints: Do not keep time-seeded placement for user-created notes.
Do not close the create flow on silent failure.

context.notes: Note capture is in primary chrome and reveals real stickies on the canvas with visible success feedback instead of silent off-screen placement.

tasks.notes: Partial slice landed: `New note` is in primary chrome, created notes use viewport-aware placement, the app retries reveal after save, and the user gets explicit success/error recovery messaging instead of a silent no-op. Still needs live viewport proof.

tasks.title: Design UI: make the facilitator a persona dock with autonomy cues
tasks.goal: Represent the facilitator as a compact bottom-left persona dock with one live line, a visible autonomy dial, explicit pause/cool-down/nudge/log controls, a hairline idle bar, and role/backoff cues while keeping AI output on the canvas.
tasks.comment: The dock is the robot's face, not the robot's workspace. It must expose the autonomy dial and role state directly on canvas, and it must show when the facilitator is waiting, thinking, capped, or stepping back.
definition_of_done: The facilitator is visible as a compact persona dock anchored to the canvas, not as a large telemetry card stack.
The dock communicates one active thought and exposes a minimal action set such as pause, cool down, nudge, turn log, and Undo robot.
The autonomy dial is reachable from anywhere on the canvas in two clicks or less and shows configured ceiling versus effective mode distinctly when they differ.
The dock shows the active role inline and pairs the idle-gate progress bar with text so timing is teachable even under reduced motion.
When caps or throttles apply, the dock surfaces a calm inline state such as holding thoughts in notes instead of using a popup or tray.
constraints: Do not reintroduce a chat-like dock with scrolling transcript.
Do not move AI voice into large chrome surfaces when it should be attached to the board.
Do not bury the autonomy dial in Settings or any secondary preference screen.

context.notes: A persona dock exists, but it is not yet visually or structurally aligned with the screenshot target. The reference dock is a compact hand-drawn control surface with very specific composition and weight.

tasks.notes: Partial slice landed: the facilitator card now leads with identity, current action, next action, and a compact readout while session-peer detail stays lower in the rail. Still needs viewport-proof closeout with bo-042.

tasks.title: Design UI: replace connection forms with canvas-first link mode
tasks.goal: Make connection authoring happen through the board itself with toolbar link mode, line hover rationale, and direct idea highlighting instead of a form-heavy rail workflow.
tasks.comment: The design reference creates connections from the toolbar and the canvas, not from a persistent side-panel composer.
definition_of_done: Users can enter a clear link mode from the primary chrome and connect two ideas directly on the canvas.
Connections expose kind and rationale from the board surface itself rather than depending on a persistent form panel.
The product no longer answers 'how do I add connections?' with a rail-only workflow.
constraints: Do not keep the manual connection form as the primary authoring model.
Do not hide connection meaning in a secondary panel only.

context.notes: Connection authoring moved onto the board via link mode and board-surface connection cues rather than depending on a rail-only form.

tasks.notes: Partial slice landed: the Connections surface now exposes explicit manual authoring, facilitator-assisted discovery, and saved-link inspection/highlighting. The composer also stays collapsed until at least two notes exist so it does not crowd the primary rail. UI-path proof is still open.

tasks.title: Design UI: prove the critical workflows on real viewport sizes
tasks.goal: Add explicit verification for the critical board workflows using the design-gap quality checklist so the UI is not marked ready until the must-haves are proven on real viewports and both themes.
tasks.comment: The design batch cannot close on screenshots or builds. The quality checklist from the gap prompt is now the sign-off contract.
definition_of_done: There is a runnable or at least deterministic verification checklist covering 1280x800, 1440x900, and a representative mobile viewport in both themes.
The checklist proves the design-gap must-haves: autonomy dial, Insight Feed, bead strip, AI Undo, turn-log pagination/filtering, discard pile, docs paperclip, rules ribbon, and reduced-motion path.
The checklist verifies visible AI-origin markers, no emoji/gradients/Shadcn-card regressions, and role-language compliance on user-visible surfaces.
The tracker is not returned to complete until this proof is attached to the close-out.
constraints: Do not count typecheck and build alone as UI proof.
Do not close the design batch without validating the real interaction path and the design-gap checklist.
expected_changes: tracker notes or docs for verification

context.notes: Typecheck and build:web pass. Whiteboard screenshots exist for desktop and mobile, but final multi-viewport and both-theme sign-off is intentionally deferred until the broader web surface is ready.

tasks.notes: Partial slice landed: added a deterministic viewport checklist covering facilitator reachability, note creation, connections, and facilitator legibility on 1280x800, 1440x900, and 390x844. The checklist exists, but it has not yet been executed on the live app, so proof is still open.

Real viewport proof started, but the 390px mobile shell still overflows horizontally and sketch-theme automation is not worth blocking broader web readiness. tasks.title: Design UI: move AI output onto the canvas as spatial artifacts and candidate ideas
tasks.goal: Render AI work as candidate ideas, anchored critiques, origin-marked connections, and other spatial artifacts on the canvas with visible provenance, confidence, and strength instead of summarizing it in chrome.
tasks.comment: This row now owns provenance and visual trust, not just spatial placement. AI and user output cannot look interchangeable once committed.
definition_of_done: Scout output appears as on-canvas candidate ideas or AI-authored stickies that users can admit or dismiss in place.

Every AI-authored surface has a visible origin marker: persona chip on committed AI stickies, dashed/peach styling on candidates, origin badge in turn-log rows, and a tiny persona marker plus rationale on AI connections.
Candidate ideas expose confidence visually, and the thinking-beat scratch-out or survival behavior corresponds to that confidence signal.
Critique surfaces show `Dev · Challenger`, strength dots, subtype switching for risk/assumption/counterexample when present, and explicit Dismiss and Handled actions.
Connections and cluster cues animate onto the board as first-class spatial objects rather than chrome summaries.
constraints: Do not collapse AI output into status text or feed-like lists.
Do not ship critique or scout output as rail cards when the board can own it.
Do not let committed AI ideas become visually indistinguishable from user-authored ideas.

context.notes: AI artifacts exist on the board, but they do not yet resemble the screenshot target. The references use irregular paper surfaces, speech-bubble critiques, dashed scouts, and much stronger spatial/visual distinction than the current branch.

tasks.title: Design UI: add per-idea turn log as an on-demand right panel
tasks.goal: Replace generic history affordances with the reference turn log: a per-idea right-side inspector opened on demand, paginated and filterable, with origin badges plus pin, dismiss, and transfer actions.
tasks.comment: The turn log is history for one idea. It is not the robot's inbox, and it cannot stay a flat unbounded list if AI roles are writing into it regularly.
definition_of_done: A selected idea can open an idea-scoped turn log on the right.
Turn log entries expose origin, rationale, and transfer/pin/dismiss actions with mono origin badges.
The log pages in 20 at a time with a `Load earlier` affordance and filter chips for All, AI, User, Critique, and Edit.
Transfer-to-board creates a new sticky near the current idea rather than replacing the idea or writing into a transcript.
The turn log stays distinct from any Shadow-mode Robot's Notes or Insight Feed staging surface.
constraints: Do not turn the turn log into a global chat transcript.
Do not keep a permanent right rail for the same information.
Do not treat an unpaginated flat list as sufficient once multiple roles are writing turns.

context.notes: A right-side turn log exists, but the current panel does not yet match the screenshot target in layout, row design, density, or overall visual treatment. Treat the provided screenshots as the design contract here.

tasks.title: Design UI: apply the notebook design system to board primitives
tasks.goal: Bring the live app onto the reference visual language with strict theme parity, forbidden-trope enforcement, reduced-motion support, and typography that keeps board content hand-drawn while longer UI copy stays readable.
tasks.comment: This row is no longer just about making the board prettier. It owns theme parity, reduced motion, and the ban on stock dashboard tropes.
definition_of_done: Board primitives visually resemble the reference stickies and paper surfaces rather than generic cards.
Both `theme-sketch` and `theme-whiteboard` render correctly from one token system with no component drift between themes.
The active typography and color tokens come from the design system rather than default app chrome conventions, and longer UI paragraphs use Inter rather than hand-drawn fonts.
Reduced-motion behavior is implemented globally for the thinking beat, scratch-outs, and connection reveals.
No gradients, emoji affordances, Shadcn-style accent cards, or other forbidden tropes remain in the live board surface.
constraints: Do not keep system-ui/Inter as the primary live board language.
Do not introduce new colors or stock dashboard treatments outside the reference system.
Do not rely on motion alone to communicate state.

context.notes: Theme infrastructure exists, but the current sketch/whiteboard rendering is still far from the provided references. The screenshots show the real target language: irregular sticky shapes, notebook/grid background, typography, borders, shadows, and panel treatment.

tasks.blocker_reason: Notebook visual system and reduced-motion work landed, but strict cross-theme parity/sign-off is deferred with bo-042 instead of continuing the proof rabbit hole.

tasks.title: WebMCP: remount lifecycle tools per selected idea and bead phase
tasks.goal: Split W3 tool registration into global board tools, lifecycle-scoped bead tools, and facilitator/control-plane coordination verbs keyed to the selected idea and phase so the active subset mounts and unmounts deterministically.
tasks.comment: Global board tools, facilitator control-plane tools, and selected-idea lifecycle tools now mount under separate WebMCP controllers, with lifecycle remount keyed to the selected idea and current phase.
definition_of_done: W3 registers global board tools under one controller, lifecycle-scoped bead tools under a controller keyed to selected idea and phase, and facilitator/control-plane coordination verbs under an explicit scoped path rather than ad hoc globals.
The scope of each bead-contract verb is explicit in code and registration docs: global, lifecycle, or facilitator/control-plane.
Bead-local tools mount and unmount as selection or phase changes without stale registrations.
Lifecycle and facilitator writes continue to use the dispatch-and-wait handshake rather than the coarse ideasChanged refresh event.
constraints: Do not introduce a second phase source of truth; derive from the existing idea phase and SUB_PHASES model.
Do not bypass the event handshake for lifecycle writes.

context.notes: Restored explicit lifecycle-scoped registration without introducing a second phase source of truth. Lifecycle writes still use the existing dispatch-and-wait handshake via the app event layer.

tasks.title: Facilitator policy: autonomy, rolling trust, and auto-backoff
tasks.goal: Implement the policy outputs that derive configured ceiling versus effective mode, track recent AI outcomes, choose commit-versus-stage behavior, and throttle the robot from Active to Guided or Shadow when the team repeatedly rejects it.
tasks.comment: Completed. The facilitator now tracks a configured ceiling versus effective mode, records rolling AI action outcomes, throttles itself down to cooldown/shadow behavior after rejection pressure, and exposes that backoff state through the dock and WebMCP autonomy tools instead of silently changing behavior.
definition_of_done: The product exposes explicit facilitation levels and tracks both configured ceiling and effective autonomy state.
A rolling window records recent autonomous actions and their accept or reject outcomes.
Policy outputs decide whether a proposal executes, stages, or drops based on effective mode, confidence/strength, and recent reception.
Passive Observer always stages; Guided Co-Pilot stages unless confidence is high and the board is idle; Active Challenger can commit lower-confidence outputs within the design contract.
Background beats visibly announce read-the-room backoff and cap states to the UI rather than silently changing behavior.
constraints: Cooldown must not stop listening or generation; it only throttles execution.
Backoff must be reversible via explicit pull, phase advance, or renewed acceptance.

context.notes: Depends on the control-plane row because autonomy/backoff is policy behavior, not a separate architectural layer.

tasks.title: Facilitator UI: build Shadow Mode Insight Feed / Robot's Notes
tasks.goal: Stage AI-generated proposals into a passive Insight Feed / Robot's Notes surface when the facilitator cools down, with labeled intent, explicit actions, passive signaling, and no forced canvas mutation.
tasks.comment: Completed. Shadow-mode staging now has a dock-accessible Robot's Notes surface backed by shared staged-insight state; automated scout/critique/connection passes can stage into notes instead of mutating the canvas, and staged notes can be applied or dismissed from the dock.
definition_of_done: Staged pending insights persist per board or phase with labels such as Tool Suggestion, Web Context, Grouping Proposal, Critique Draft, Scout Draft, and Connection Draft.
The UI exposes a collapsible Robot's Notes / Insight Feed surface from the persona dock, and it never auto-opens itself.
Passive signaling uses a bead badge and/or dock glow, not a popup or notification tray.
Acting on an item reuses the mapped verbs: Admit, Elaborate, Attach, Group, Shelve, or Dismiss.
Accepting an insight counts as positive signal for autonomy recovery.
constraints: Do not hide staged insights in a generic history panel.
Do not discard suppressed AI proposals when Shadow mode is active.
Do not implement Shadow mode as a notification tray or modal inbox.

context.notes: Tightened to match the gap prompt's required labels, actions, and passive signaling rules.

tasks.title: History: add AI Undo over AI-authored change sets
tasks.goal: Expose a targeted AI Undo path for recent AI-authored mutations with a dedicated dock affordance, change-specific tooltip, and skip-over logic for later user-authored changes.
tasks.comment: Completed. AI Undo now finds the latest safe AI-authored change set, previews it in the dock, and applies a scoped inverse as a new change set without rewinding later unrelated user changes.
definition_of_done: Recent AI-authored changes are identifiable in history and reversible without manual archaeology.
The persona dock exposes an `Undo robot` or equivalent affordance that is enabled only when an AI-origin change can be reverted safely.
The affordance previews the specific change that will be reverted.
The reversal path skips over later user-authored changes rather than rewinding them as collateral.
The reversal path does not interfere with generic undo/redo semantics.
constraints: Do not build a second history store.
Do not rely on generic full-history undo as the only recovery path.

context.notes: Must-have per the design-gap contract, so promoted to p0.

tasks.title: Facilitation UI: add derived 12-bead bead string
tasks.goal: Render the 12 micro-phases as a compact derived bead string over SUB_PHASES, with locked, active, completed, needs-attention, and soft-nudge states plus detail-on-click behavior.
tasks.comment: The bead string is the visual language that makes the 12-step machine legible to humans. The prompt now makes the five bead states explicit, so the row must enforce them.
definition_of_done: The bead string is derived from the existing phase state, not stored as a second workflow model.
The strip renders all five required states: locked, active, completed, needs_attention, and soft_nudge.
The strip is compact and persistent at the canvas edge rather than becoming a workflow wizard.
Clicking a completed bead opens recorded state such as lenses, challenges, rules, or stress tests without creating a parallel transition path.
Soft cues from suggest_next_bead and flag_bead_for_review surface visually without changing phase; advance_phase remains the only hard transition.
constraints: Do not create a second phase state store or a separate slide_bead mutation path.
Do not let the bead string turn back into a sidebar workflow wizard.

context.notes: The derived bead strip is rendered on the board surface and driven from the canonical bead-state helper.

tasks.title: Design UI: replace prototype beat language with role language on live surfaces
tasks.goal: Remove user-visible prototype beat terminology from the W3 UI and replace it with the role system vocabulary so the live product speaks in roles, not demo beats.
tasks.comment: The current live UI still leaks `Scout beat`, `Board Beats`, and related prototype terminology. The design contract says role language is the source of truth.
definition_of_done: User-visible surfaces use `Scout`, `Synthesizer`, `Challenger`, `Historian`, and `Facilitator` instead of prototype beat names.
The persona dock shows the active role inline.
Any remaining internal `beat` naming is hidden from the user or intentionally limited to implementation-only code paths.
Cluster and summarise stop reading like separate public beats; they are presented as role outputs or facilitator actions.
constraints: Do not rename durable/internal implementation identifiers if doing so would create risky churn with no user-visible benefit.
Do not leave visible prototype beat copy in cards, labels, or status pills once the role system is in place.

context.notes: Visible prototype beat language was replaced with role/facilitator language on live surfaces, and stray tool-surface copy was cleaned up as well.

tasks.title: Design UI: make supporting docs first-class on idea cards
tasks.goal: Show supporting-doc state directly on every idea card with a paperclip pill and idea-anchored docs popover, and allow docs to be attached from the card or from staged Insight Feed items.
tasks.comment: Docs already affect reasoning, but the surface is still too detached from the idea itself. The design contract requires docs to be visible at the point of thought.
definition_of_done: Every idea card shows a supporting-doc count pill using a real paperclip glyph, not emoji.
Clicking the pill opens a compact docs popover anchored to the idea rather than a global modal.
Docs can be attached from the idea surface and from Insight Feed suggestions such as `Attach to Idea X?`.
The docs surface stays lightweight enough to remain part of the canvas workflow rather than pulling the user into a settings-style flow.
constraints: Do not hide supporting docs behind a global modal as the primary path.
Do not use emoji as the paperclip affordance.

context.notes: Supporting docs are first-class on idea cards and in the idea-scoped docs panel rather than hidden behind generic history chrome.

tasks.title: Design UI: align the discard pile to the bottom-left drawer contract
tasks.goal: Turn the discard pile into the required bottom-left drawer with count, compact recall list, restore-to-position behavior, and explicit compatibility with Historian-driven revive suggestions.
tasks.comment: The repo already has discard primitives, but the design contract makes this a specific spatial drawer pattern tied to recall and revive behavior.
definition_of_done: Discarded ideas live in a bottom-left drawer with a visible count and collapsible list.
Restoring an idea returns it to its last known position with a brief re-entry animation rather than dropping it arbitrarily.
The drawer coexists cleanly with the persona dock and does not force a relayout.
Historian or Insight Feed revive prompts can target the same drawer/restore flow without hard-deleting discarded context.
constraints: Do not hard-delete discarded ideas.
Do not hide the discard pile in an unrelated side panel or settings screen.

context.notes: Discard pile is aligned to the bottom-left drawer contract with restore affordances on the board surface.

tasks.title: Facilitation UI: add the must-stay-true rules ribbon
tasks.goal: Surface must-stay-true rules as a pinned top-of-canvas ribbon with overflow, provenance, and remove affordances so the Facilitator's constraints remain visible after bead 3.
tasks.comment: Rules are not side notes. They feed every later phase prompt, so the board needs a persistent visual home for them.
definition_of_done: A pinned ribbon at the top of the canvas shows must-stay-true rules with max 5 visible and an overflow affordance.
Each rule is a compact chip with short text, origin badge, and a remove affordance.
Adding or removing rules is wired to the lifecycle tool path rather than being trapped in the workspace fallback UI only.
The ribbon remains visible during later beads so stress tests and readiness decisions have an explicit shared constraint surface.
constraints: Do not hide must-stay-true rules only inside the form-driven workspace flow.
Do not turn the rules ribbon into a modal or a sidebar list.

context.notes: Must-stay-true rules are visible as a board-top ribbon with overflow handling and edit/remove affordances.

tasks.title: Facilitator control plane: add Policy Engine and Trigger Matrix
tasks.goal: Introduce an explicit Facilitator Policy Engine that watches board/workflow context, selects the managerial role, and decides whether each candidate action should execute, stage, or be blocked.
tasks.comment: The facilitator now runs through an explicit policy engine that builds control-plane context, classifies facilitation verbs, selects a managerial role, and decides whether the next action should execute, stage, or stay blocked.
definition_of_done: There is an explicit facilitator context shape spanning board state, bead state, discarded memory, supporting docs, recent AI outcomes, idle/user activity, and relevant W1 context when available.
A policy engine answers four questions for every candidate action: should the robot act, which role should act, should the result execute or stage, and how strong the intervention should be.
A trigger matrix exists for Scout, Synthesizer, Challenger, Historian, and Facilitator with priorities, cooldowns, and execute-versus-stage defaults.

Every facilitation verb is classified as one of: hard transition, durable mutation, soft facilitation signal, or read-only derived state, and policy consumes that classification instead of treating all tools the same.

The default execution stance is proposal-first rather than mutation-first, with directional or interruptive interventions usually staged before mutation unless the current policy explicitly allows execution.
The control plane does not create a second workflow engine and does not bypass WebMCP verbs or human override paths.
constraints: Do not model the robot as a generic assistant detached from the board.
Do not introduce hidden phase transitions or a second workflow state machine.
Do not let the control plane mutate the board outside explicit tool/event execution or staged insight surfaces.

context.notes: Policy metadata now rides with AI-authored facilitator events, and the observer loop consumes policy decisions before dispatching board mutations.

tasks.title: Bead/tool contract: ambiguity management verbs
tasks.goal: Implement `list_ambiguities` and `resolve_ambiguity` as explicit lifecycle verbs for beads 0 and 1 so ambiguity state is readable, actionable, and no longer trapped inside prompts or passive brief fields.
tasks.comment: Execution started in parallel with bo-059. Ambiguity state is being pulled out of prompt-only flow into explicit read/write lifecycle verbs and handshake-backed mutations.
definition_of_done: `list_ambiguities` is a lifecycle-scoped read-only tool for the selected idea and returns the current ambiguity set for beads 0 and 1 with severity, resolution mode, and resolution state.
`resolve_ambiguity` is a lifecycle-scoped durable mutation that records how a specific ambiguity was resolved, deferred, or left open, using the handshake path rather than a bare refresh event.
The source of truth is explicit board/idea state rather than inferred prompt text alone, and clarification questions remain linked back to ambiguity ids.
Ambiguity state appears in the bead detail / phase inspector and contributes to turn-log or phase-history visibility.
AI-authored ambiguity resolutions are attributable and reversible through normal history / AI Undo paths.
constraints: Do not treat answered clarification text alone as a proxy for resolved ambiguity state.
Do not add a second ambiguity store outside the idea/board source of truth.

context.notes: Explicit ambiguity read/write verbs now operate on board-backed idea state, expose linked clarification context, surface ambiguity state in the active workspace flow, and emit attributable change sets that feed derived phase history.

tasks.title: Bead/tool contract: rule management verbs
tasks.goal: Implement `add_rule` and `remove_rule` as explicit lifecycle verbs for bead 3 and later beads so must-stay-true constraints are durable, operable, and shared outside the fallback flow.
tasks.comment: Completed. add_rule and remove_rule are lifecycle-scoped durable mutation verbs with handshake-backed completion, shared briefState.mustStayTrueRules state, and canvas-first rule editing/review via the active rules bead.
definition_of_done: `add_rule` and `remove_rule` are lifecycle-scoped durable mutation verbs with explicit schemas and bead ownership centered on bead 3.
The source of truth is `briefState.mustStayTrueRules`, and both the ribbon UI and bead detail read the same state.
Rule writes use the dispatch-and-wait handshake, record actor provenance, and do not rely on the workspace fallback form as the only edit path.
The rules ribbon and later bead inspectors can add, remove, and review rules without leaving the canvas-first flow.
AI-authored rule mutations are attributable and reversible through normal history / AI Undo paths.
constraints: Do not leave `confirm_rules` as the only structured path for editing rules.
Do not hide rule management inside a modal, rail card, or fallback inspector-only flow.

context.notes: Makes must-stay-true rules a first-class lifecycle grammar instead of a one-shot phase artifact.

tasks.title: Bead/tool contract: risk management verbs
tasks.goal: Implement `list_risks` and `patch_risk` as explicit lifecycle verbs for beads 4 and 4.5 so premortem output becomes tracked risk state rather than static critique text.
tasks.comment: Completed. list_risks and patch_risk are lifecycle-scoped read/write verbs over briefState.risks, the active premortem/stress surface now exposes an editable risk register, and phase history records follow-up-note risk edits as durable lifecycle changes.
definition_of_done: `list_risks` is a lifecycle-scoped read-only tool that returns the current risk set for the selected idea with the metadata needed for beads 4 and 4.5.
`patch_risk` is a lifecycle-scoped durable mutation for editing risk fields and follow-up annotations, and it uses the handshake path rather than a bare refresh.
The source of truth is explicit board/idea risk state plus stress linkage, not freeform critique text or fallback-only notes.
Risk changes appear in premortem/stress detail and phase-history visibility so the facilitator can explain why a review or challenge is still open.
AI-authored risk mutations are attributable and reversible through normal history / AI Undo paths.
constraints: Do not collapse risk state into critique cards or board comments only.
